account: Brazil's Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) launched VitórIA on 17 May 2023 under Resolution 800/2023. The court's artificial-intelligence advisory unit built it with the information-technology and precedents offices. The STF uses VitorIA, operational since 2023, to compare the texts of incoming appeals. It groups cases that raise similar legal questions for the staff who screen candidates for repercussão geral themes. The court says that the tool does not judge cases. In her manifestation of 8 August 2023 in ARE 1441934, the leading case of Tema 1.261 on municipal teachers' personal pay advantages, President Rosa Weber wrote that the precedents office had used VitórIA to identify and monitor at least 247 similar appeals by semantic-similarity clustering. The theme record shows that the Plenary decided unanimously on 22 August 2023 that there is no general repercussion because the question is infraconstitutional. The decision became final on 23 September 2023. No cited source says what then happened to the 247 appeals. On 28 September 2026 the STF described the controversy behind Tema 1.261. It said that VitorIA identified at least 247 appeals with similar legal questions by grouping on content similarity. The STF added that finding so many similar cases did not determine the result. The STF credits VitorIA with four themes in 2023, 19 in 2024 and 11 in 2025. It says that these figures do not refer to decisions taken with AI help and do not allow calculating accuracy or time saved.

ai_role.statement: The President's manifestation of 8 August 2023 states that the court's precedents office used VitórIA to identify and monitor the 247 appeals by semantic-similarity clustering. The President then judged that the question had strong potential for repetition and proposed that the Plenary find no general repercussion, which it did. The STF's 2026 statement adds that finding so many similar cases did not determine the result. The court's AI advisory unit built the tool with its IT and precedents offices, so the developer and the deployer are the same body. No source measures time saved or accuracy.

fields.account: Brazil's Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) launched VitórIA on 17 May 2023 under Resolution 800/2023. The court's artificial-intelligence advisory unit built it with the information-technology and precedents offices. The STF uses VitorIA, operational since 2023, to compare the texts of incoming appeals. It groups cases that raise similar legal questions for the staff who screen candidates for repercussão geral themes. The court says that the tool does not judge cases. In her manifestation of 8 August 2023 in ARE 1441934, the leading case of Tema 1.261 on municipal teachers' personal pay advantages, President Rosa Weber wrote that the precedents office had used VitórIA to identify and monitor at least 247 similar appeals by semantic-similarity clustering. The theme record shows that the Plenary decided unanimously on 22 August 2023 that there is no general repercussion because the question is infraconstitutional. The decision became final on 23 September 2023. No cited source says what then happened to the 247 appeals. On 28 September 2026 the STF described the controversy behind Tema 1.261. It said that VitorIA identified at least 247 appeals with similar legal questions by grouping on content similarity. The STF added that finding so many similar cases did not determine the result. The STF credits VitorIA with four themes in 2023, 19 in 2024 and 11 in 2025. It says that these figures do not refer to decisions taken with AI help and do not allow calculating accuracy or time saved.
